cards.meaning: lscpu = what chips you have; mpstat / sar = how busy each core is
cards.notes: Architecture vs utilization

cards.meaning: CPU architecture: sockets, cores, threads, NUMA, vendor, model name
cards.notes: Inventory for sizing VMs and taskset — not live busyness

cards.meaning: Logical processors the OS sees
cards.notes: The number you check against sockets × cores × threads

cards.meaning: 1 = no extra hyperthread visible; 2 = SMT
cards.notes: Part of the logical-CPU formula

cards.meaning: Physical cores on one CPU package
cards.notes: Multiply by sockets and threads for logical CPUs

cards.meaning: CPU packages on the board
cards.notes: Part of the inventory math

cards.meaning: Memory domains — cores are closer to some RAM than other
cards.notes: RAM is not equally far from every socket

cards.meaning: Approximately equals logical CPU(s) the OS reports
cards.notes: Check inventory math against the CPU(s) line in lscpu

cards.meaning: Display CPU statistics of an individual CPU (or core)
cards.notes: Default report is CPU utilization if you do not pick another activity type

cards.meaning: Per-CPU utilization for every logical CPU plus a summary line all
cards.notes: No interval = stats since system startup (boot) — a long average, not "right now"

cards.meaning: Stats since system startup (boot) — long average, not live
cards.notes: To sample now, give an interval and count

cards.meaning: Live samples: every 1 second, 5 times
cards.notes: Same interval/count pattern as sar

cards.meaning: User-space process CPU time
cards.notes: Application work, not kernel

cards.meaning: Niced (low-priority) user time
cards.notes: User time at nice priority

cards.meaning: Kernel CPU time
cards.notes: System/kernel work

cards.meaning: Idle waiting for disk/network I/O
cards.notes: High %iowait → storage problem, not "need more CPU"

cards.meaning: Hardware / software interrupt CPU time
cards.notes: Interrupt handling overhead

cards.meaning: Time a hypervisor took from this VM
cards.notes: High %steal → noisy neighbor on the hypervisor

cards.meaning: Time running a guest (KVM host)
cards.notes: Host side of virtualization

cards.meaning: CPU has nothing to do
cards.notes: Idle high = bored; iowait high = waiting on I/O

cards.meaning: Display per-CPU statistics; often from collected history, can also sample live
cards.notes: Often installed with sysstat; can replay /var/log/sa/ historical data

cards.meaning: Per-CPU stats: all processors, interval 1 second, count 1 sample
cards.notes: Wait 1s, print once. Same utilization story as mpstat, plus history when collection is enabled

cards.meaning: Report all processors plus the all average line
cards.notes: Same idea as mpstat -P ALL

cards.meaning: First number = sample interval in seconds; second = how many samples
cards.notes: 1 1 means wait 1s, print once

cards.front: sar/mpstat all vs a single CPU line
cards.meaning: all is the average; individual CPU lines show per-core busyness
cards.example: CPU 0 at 35% user while another core is idle 100%
cards.notes: Core 0 can be busier than the all average
